text: manifest script verbatim; one request per clip; no previous/next text

clips.script: First.
Next.
And last.
Phone face down. Silence your notifications, then keep your phone face down or in your pocket unless a part asks you to use it.
Name what’s on. In a few words, jot down what’s taking up the most room in your head right now.
Open a window. Open a window or a door, and take a moment to look outside before you begin.
Stand and reach. Stand up and reach both arms overhead, only as high as is comfortable, then lower them slowly. Three or four times.
Put a song on. Put on a song you really like, and let it play while you start.
A comfortable spot. Find somewhere comfortable to sit or lie, and let your shoulders drop.
Look around. Look slowly around you, and find three things you hadn’t noticed before.
Move to music. Put on songs with a bit of life in them, and move however feels good — sway, step, walk around the room.
Standing stretch. Reach up, bend to each side, roll your shoulders, twist gently, then march on the spot. Only as far as is comfortable.
One active job. One job that keeps you on your feet — sweeping, hoovering, carrying things — at a pace that feels comfortable.
A brisk walk. Head out. Start easy, then walk briskly — at a pace you can still talk at. Turn back about halfway.
Round the block. Step outside and walk once round the block, at whatever pace feels right today.
Quick clear-up. Pick one room and put things back where they live. Don’t sort — just put away what’s out.
Some fresh air. Step outside, or stand at an open door or window, for a few minutes. Look around and take in what’s there.
Get it out. Write down everything on your mind, without sorting. When you run dry, ask what else is nagging at you.
Clear one corner. One corner of a desk, one drawer or one shelf: take everything off, then put back only what belongs there.
One task, no switching. Pick one task on your mind and put everything else out of sight. Stay with it until the time’s up — finished or not.
Listen to one thing. Put on one album, episode or recording, then put your phone face down. Nothing else to do but listen.
Read a few pages. Read what you’re reading, or anything nearby. If your mind wanders, reread the last line.
Screen-free walk. Silence your notifications and keep your phone in your pocket. Walk easily, and look around you rather than at a screen.
Set screens aside. Minimise what you don’t need on your screens — nothing needs closing. Keep in view only what comes next.
Look far away. Let your eyes settle on the furthest thing you can comfortably see — through a window, or across the room.
A slow warm drink. Make a warm drink you’d enjoy. Hold the cup in both hands, and drink it slowly, with your phone face down.
Gentle stretch. Slowly: neck, shoulders, open the chest, a seated twist, then fold forward and come up slowly. Only what’s comfortable.
Neck and shoulders. Gently tip your head towards each shoulder. Then lift your shoulders to your ears and let them drop.
Quiet music. Somewhere comfortable, put on something quiet. Close your eyes if you like, and let one song run into the next.
Easy walk. Step outside without picking a route. Walk slower than usual, and stop for anything that catches your eye.
Sit outside. Find somewhere outside to sit, with your phone in your pocket. Listen to what you can hear, near and far.
Tend to one thing. Pick one small thing to look after — a plant, a bedside table, a shelf — and go slower than you would in a hurry.
Choose one thing. Look over what you wrote, and circle the one thing that matters most next.
Write the first step. For the thing you circled, write the very first small step — small enough to start with.
Sit for a minute. Sit still for a minute or two before you move on. There’s nothing to do.
Put things back. Put back anything that’s out of place nearby, and leave your space ready for later.
A glass of water. Pour a glass of water and drink it before you carry on.
Shake it out. Shake out your hands and arms loosely, then let them rest.
Choose what’s next. Decide the one thing you’ll do next, and go to it.
Note one thing. Note down one small thing from today you’d like to remember.
One long reach. Finish with one long reach overhead, as far as is comfortable, then let your arms drop.
That’s your Circle. Take a moment before you move on.
